gamps_law.wizards_and_beasts.life_creati: To create life is beyond the reach of magic. Even the darkest wizard cannot overrule this law.
gamps_law.wizards_and_beasts.love_conjur: Love cannot be conjured. What this magic can imitate is obsession, and obsession is not love.

bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.knarl.name: Knarl
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.knarl.short_: A wary hedgehog-like beast that treats kindness as a trap.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.knarl.full_l: Indistinguishable from a hedgehog save for its behaviour, a knarl suspects any food left out to be bait and ravages the garden in retaliation.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.knarl.weakne: Left in peace, it does no harm
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.griffin.name: Griffin
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.griffin.shor: Eagle-headed, lion-bodied guardian of the heights.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.griffin.full: Fierce yet loyal to those who earn its respect, the griffin nests on remote summits and defends its eyrie with talon and beak.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.fairy.name: Fairy
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.fairy.short_: A vain, faintly glowing winged sprite of human shape.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.fairy.full_l: Possessing little magic and less sense, fairies are prized as decoration; they preen endlessly and squabble over the prettiest perch.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.puffskein.sh: A spherical, cream-furred ball of contented appetite.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.puffskein.fu: A docile companion that hums when happy and extends a long pink tongue to feast on leftovers, bogeys and stray insects alike.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pygmy_puff.s: A miniature, brightly dyed Puffskein bred as a pet.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pygmy_puff.f: A Weasley creation in pink and purple, the Pygmy Puff is small enough to ride a shoulder and trills softly for affection.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.chizpurfle.h: On the fur and feathers of larger beasts; in wand cores
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.chizpurfle.s: A tiny fanged parasite that gnaws magic itself.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.chizpurfle.f: Barely a millimetre long but armed with great fangs, chizpurfles infest magical creatures and even chew their way into wands to feast on residual magic.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.horklump.sho: A pink, bristle-covered fungus-beast rooted in the earth.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.horklump.ful: Resembling a fleshy mushroom, the horklump sends sinewy feelers underground to catch earthworms and spreads across a garden within days.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.red_cap.name: Red Cap
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.red_cap.shor: A squat, goblin-like horror that hunts the unwary.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.red_cap.full: Dwelling where blood has been spilled, red caps cudgel lone travellers to death after dark, dyeing their caps afresh.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.red_cap.weak: Driven off by charms and light
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.erkling.name: Erkling
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.erkling.shor: An elfish creature that lures children with enchanting song.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.erkling.full: Three feet tall with a pointed face, the erkling sings a beguiling cackle to entice children close, then carries them off to eat.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.leprechaun.s: A mischievous green sprite that conjures vanishing gold.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.leprechaun.f: Cleverer than fairies and fond of pranks, the leprechaun produces realistic gold that dissolves to nothing within hours.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.wampus_cat.s: A great panther-like cat of immense magical power.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.wampus_cat.f: Sacred to the Cherokee and faster than an arrow, the wampus cat can walk upright and hypnotise with its yellow eyes; its hair makes a potent wand core.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.salamander.s: A small fire-dwelling lizard born of flame.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.salamander.f: A salamander lives only as long as the fire that birthed it burns, feeding on flame and exuding a milky substance that cures burns.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.salamander.w: Dies if its fire goes out
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.murtlap.name: Murtlap
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.murtlap.shor: A rat-like beast with a sea-anemone growth on its back.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.murtlap.full: The pickled growths of a murtlap are eaten for resistance to curses, and its essence soothes cuts and stings.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.moke.name: Moke
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.moke.short_l: A silver-green lizard that shrinks from danger.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.moke.full_lo: A moke can contract its body at will, vanishing from sight; its prized shrinking skin makes a thief-proof money pouch.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.jarvey.name: Jarvey
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.jarvey.short: An oversized ferret with a foul, talking mouth.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.jarvey.full_: A jarvey speaks only in short, mostly rude bursts as it tears through gnome and rodent burrows in a constant temper.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.kappa.name: Kappa
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.kappa.short_: A monkey-like water demon that drains blood.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.kappa.full_l: The kappa carries water in a hollow on its head and strangles waders; it is bound by courtesy and will bow back if bowed to, spilling its water and its strength.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.kappa.weakne: Tricked into bowing out its water
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.gnome.name: Gnome
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.gnome.full_l: A common nuisance dug from flower beds and flung over the hedge, the garden gnome bites with surprisingly sharp teeth.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.gnome.weakne: Dizzied and thrown out by hand
A horse before, a great fish behind.
The hippocampus draws merpeople's sea-chariots; gentle but powerful, it lays large, semi-transparent eggs in warm shallows.
A vast, horse-headed serpent of the deep.
Reaching a hundred feet, the sea serpent rears in great coils from the waves; for all its fearsome look, no human death is recorded by its hand.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.fire_crab.sh: A jewelled tortoise-crab that returns fire with fire.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.fire_crab.fu: Its bejewelled shell is so prized that the beast is protected; when threatened it blasts flame from its rear.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.imp.name: Imp
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.imp.short_lo: A small slapstick prankster of the riverbanks
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.imp.full_lor: Less clever than a pixie and fond of crude tricks, the imp trips and shoves travellers along boggy paths.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.porlock.name: Porlock
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.porlock.habi: Grassy plains of Dorset and southern Ireland
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.porlock.shor: A shaggy, hoof-footed guardian of horses.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.porlock.full: Shy and clad in rough hair, the porlock hides among a herd it has chosen to protect and distrusts humans utterly.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.nogtail.name: Nogtail
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.nogtail.habi: Farms and pig sties of Europe and America
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.nogtail.shor: A demon piglet that blights a farm from within.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.nogtail.full: Suckling among a litter unseen, the nogtail dooms a farm to ruin unless chased beyond its bounds by a pure-white dog.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.nogtail.weak: Banished only by a white dog
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.dugbog.name: Dugbog
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.dugbog.habit: Marshes and bogs of Europe and the Americas
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.dugbog.short: A log-like marsh lurker that ruins crops.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.dugbog.full_: Resembling dead wood until it moves, the dugbog savages the legs of passers-by and feasts on Mandrake roots.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.dugbog.weakn: Gives itself away when it moves
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.mackled_mala: A spiny, lobster-like land beast whose bite breeds bad luck.
Its bite leaves the victim intensely unlucky for up to a week, so wounds must never be gambled on.
Inflicts a week of bad luck
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ramora.name: Ramora
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ramora.short: A silver fish that anchors ships and guards them.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ramora.full_: Possessing powerful magic, the ramora can hold a vessel motionless in the water and is protected by the International Confederation of Wizards.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.shrake.name: Shrake
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.shrake.short: A wholly spine-covered fish that shreds nets.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.shrake.full_: Created to spite rude Muggle fishermen, the shrake's spines tear any net it passes through, ruining a catch.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.tebo.name: Tebo
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.tebo.short_l: An ash-grey warthog that turns invisible.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.tebo.full_lo: Able to vanish at will, the tebo is a dangerous and elusive beast whose hide is valued for shields and protective gear.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hodag.name: Hodag
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hodag.short_: A horned, frog-faced beast that drinks dreams.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hodag.full_l: About the size of a large dog with great horns, the hodag is friendly to wizards and drains the blood of Snallygasters as it roams by night.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.snallygaster: A part-bird, part-reptile flyer often mistaken for a dragon.
Blood-drinking and metal-toothed, the snallygaster has been glimpsed by Muggles often enough to demand constant Obliviation.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.glumbumble.s: A grey, furry flyer that drips melancholy nectar.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.glumbumble.f: The glumbumble produces a treacle that induces deep sadness, used as the antidote to Alihotsy-leaf hysteria.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pogrebin.sho: A rock-like grey demon that feeds on despair.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pogrebin.ful: Barely a foot tall, the pogrebin shadows a person until they sink into hopeless lethargy, then pounces.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.quintaped.ha: The Isle of Drear, off Scotland
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.quintaped.sh: A five-legged, blood-red carnivore with a taste for humans.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.quintaped.fu: Covered in reddish-brown hair and impossible to relocate, the highly dangerous quintaped lurks on its hidden island home.
gui.wizards_and_beasts.heritage.title: Choose Your Heritage
gui.wizards_and_beasts.heritage.confirm_: Your bloodline shapes every spell you cast and every door that opens — or closes — before you.
gui.wizards_and_beasts.heritage.nav_hint: Arrow keys to browse, Enter to confirm.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.wizardkind.l: Born to the wand and the spellbook — the most numerous of magical peoples, raised on incantations and the quiet politics of blood.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.wizardkind.f: It does not do to dwell on dreams and forget to live.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.werewolf.lor: Humans marked by lycanthropy, gifted predatory strength beneath the full moon and burdened by a world that fears the wolf within.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.werewolf.fla: The moon keeps its own calendar, and it does not negotiate.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.obscurial.lo: A witch or wizard whose suppressed magic curdled into a parasitic Obscurus — devastating power bought at a tragically short life.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.obscurial.fl: Magic denied does not vanish. It waits, and it festers.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.goblin.lore: An ancient people of metal and mathematics, masters of Gringotts' vaults and keepers of every grudge in wand law.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.goblin.flavo: They remember who truly owns the blade in your hand.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.house_elf.lo: Bound by old compulsions yet wielding domestic magic potent enough to slip wards that stop grown wizards cold.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.house_elf.fl: Give one a sock, and you may change the course of a war.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.veela.lore: Golden beings whose dance bewitches the unwary and whose fury blossoms into wings of flame.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.veela.flavor: Beauty is the bait; the fire is the truth beneath it.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.giant.lore: Colossal near-human folk of the northern ranges, thick-hided enough to shrug off spells that would fell a wizard outright.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.giant.flavor: Their laughter is mistaken for weather.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.centaur.lore: Proud half-equine forest-dwellers who scorn servitude and read the turning futures written across the stars.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.vampire.lore: Undead predators of dusk and diplomacy, their strength matched only by the old superstitions they cannot wholly escape.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.vampire.flav: Daylight is a treaty they did not sign.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.merpeople.lo: Merrows, selkies, and sirens of the cold deep, keeping their own chief, their own law, and a song that nearly drowned a champion.
heritage.wizards_and_beasts.merpeople.fl: Above the surface, our voices sound only like screams.
item.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul_slime.desc: Faintly damp residue from an attic-dwelling ghoul.
item.wizards_and_beasts.golden_snidget_f: From a near-extinct, exquisitely fast bird.
item.wizards_and_beasts.granian_hair.des: Coarse hair from the fastest winged horse breed.
item.wizards_and_beasts.horned_serpent_g: A softly glowing gem, once set in a serpent's brow.
item.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie_venom_: Potent poison, harvested with great care.
item.wizards_and_beasts.yeti_fur.desc: Thick, frost-white fur from the Himalayan Yeti.
A shimmering trace left behind by a splitting Matagot.
item.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind_shado: A wisp of the creature's own concealment.
Curved and vicious, built for a strike from behind.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul.name: Ghoul
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul.short_: A slimy, buck-toothed nuisance that lives in attics and bangs on pipes.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul.full_l: Resembling a slimy, buck-toothed ogre, the Ghoul is one of the most common — and most harmless — wizarding pests. It rarely leaves its attic, occasionally moaning or knocking on pipework, and flees rather than fights when disturbed. The Ministry's Ghoul Task Force removes strays found in Muggle homes to preserve the Statute of Secrecy.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul.abilit: Ghoul makes ambient moaning and knocking sounds.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.ghoul.threat: Almost entirely harmless — startling more than dangerous.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.golden_snidg: A near-extinct golden bird of legendary agility — the Golden Snitch's namesake.

Small, golden, and fitted with fully rotational wings, the Golden Snidget can change direction with astonishing speed. Once hunted as the original Quidditch prize, the practice was banned in 1269 after the species neared extinction; the enchanted Golden Snitch was invented as a harmless replacement. Protected ever since, a Snidget sighting is treasured, not pursued.
Golden Snidget dodges incoming attacks with uncanny reflexes.
No threat whatsoever — protected by law and instinct alike.
Nearly impossible to catch once alarmed.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.name: Granian
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.shor: A grey-green Irish winged horse, the fastest of the four recognised breeds.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.full: Native to Ireland, the Granian is prized above all other winged horse breeds for raw speed. Its coat runs from dappled grey to a distinctive greenish sheen, and a well-trained Granian can outpace nearly any other flying mount over open ground. Alongside the Abraxan and Aethonan, it completes the trio of winged horses most commonly bred by wizarding stables.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.abil: Granian is capable of sustained, exceptionally fast flight.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.thre: Skittish around strangers but not aggressive.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.granian.weak: Requires an experienced hand to approach and ride.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.horned_serpe: A river serpent bearing a luminous gem in its brow, native to North America.

A river-dwelling serpent said to be distantly related to the Basilisk, the Horned Serpent carries a glowing gem embedded in its forehead. One of the four founding creatures of Ilvermorny, it is honoured for wisdom and scholarship. Sightings near still water are considered a good omen by those who know to look for the telltale glow beneath the surface.
Horned Serpent's brow-gem emits a soft, steady glow.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie.sh: A short, grey-skinned trickster of North American folklore, armed with poisoned arrows.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie.fu: Related to European goblins but a distinct species in their own right, Pukwudgies are short, large-eared, and fiercely territorial. They favour poisoned arrows and are known to vanish and reappear at will when threatened. Wizards who show genuine respect are occasionally rewarded with an uneasy alliance — but a Pukwudgie's goodwill is never guaranteed twice.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie.ab: Pukwudgie can vanish and reappear a short distance away when struck.
Pukwudgie fires poisoned darts from range.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie.th: Genuinely dangerous in numbers — poison and hit-and-run tactics.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.pukwudgie.we: Solitary Pukwudgies are far less dangerous than a group.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.name: Yeti
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.habitat: High snowy peaks and glacial slopes.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.short_l: The Abominable Snowman of Muggle legend — very real, and very dangerous.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.full_lo: Towering and white-furred, the Yeti roams the highest reaches of the Himalayas, rated XXXX by the Ministry's Beast Division. A dedicated Yeti Task Force monitors sightings to prevent Muggle exposure. Its immense strength and biting cold aura make close combat perilous, though its pale coat offers surprisingly effective camouflage against fresh snow.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.ability: Yeti radiates a chilling aura that slows those nearby.
Immensely strong — capable of devastating knockback blows.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.yeti.weaknes: Loses its camouflage advantage once it attacks.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.rougarou.sho: A dog-headed swamp-stalker of Louisiana folklore, a regional cousin of the werewolf.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.rougarou.ful: Recognised by Pottermore's account of North American wizarding history, the Rougarou is a canine-headed curse-creature distinct from the true werewolf, though a bite carries a milder echo of the same affliction. It stalks the bayous of Louisiana in near silence, hunting alongside others of its kind when the moon is right.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.rougarou.abi: Rougarou's bite carries a chance to inflict a lingering curse.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.rougarou.thr: Hunts in packs and stalks in near silence.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.rougarou.wea: Isolated from its pack, far less coordinated.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.name: Matagot
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.shor: A French cat-spirit that splits into copies of itself when struck.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.full: Half-spirit and half-feline, the Matagot is native to French wizarding folklore and was documented among the beasts overseen by the French Ministry of Magic. Its body is partly incorporeal, letting blows pass through harmlessly, and a hard enough strike can cause it to split into smaller copies of itself rather than fall.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.abil: Matagot's incorporeal body shrugs off a portion of incoming damage.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.thre: Fighting one can unexpectedly turn into fighting several.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.matagot.weak: Individually fragile — the danger is in the numbers, not the fight.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.bundimun.sho: A creeping house pest whose secretions slowly rot wooden foundations.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.bundimun.ful: First recorded in Scotland, the Bundimun is a squat, mould-covered pest that secretes a corrosive substance capable of eating through wood and stone over time. Left unchecked, an infestation can compromise an entire structure — wizarding homeowners are advised to treat the first signs of unexplained rot with suspicion.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.bundimun.abi: Bundimun's secretions slowly corrode nearby wooden structures.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.bundimun.thr: No direct threat to a person — the danger is structural.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.bundimun.wea: Slow-moving and entirely passive when confronted.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.lobalug.name: Lobalug
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.lobalug.shor: A jellyfish-like creature of the North Sea, harmless unless provoked.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.lobalug.full: Floating and largely inert, the Lobalug drifts through the cold waters of the North Sea. Its only defence is a jet of toxic ink, prized as a potion ingredient and a component of Wartcap powder. Left alone, it poses no danger at all — provoke it, and the resulting cloud is best avoided.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.lobalug.abil: Lobalug releases a toxic ink cloud when threatened.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.lobalug.weak: Slow and defenceless once its ink is spent.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.h: Dark, dense forest, most active by night.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.s: A forest stalker invisible to anyone looking straight at it.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.f: A creature of American forest folklore, the Hidebehind is invisible to any observer who looks at it head-on — always slipping out of sight behind the nearest cover. It stalks travellers from directly behind, striking only when unseen. Its own blind spot is its weakness: a well-aimed blow from behind lands far harder than one from the front.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.a: Hidebehind is invisible to anyone facing it directly.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.t: Dangerous precisely because it is so rarely seen coming.
bestiary.wizards_and_beasts.hidebehind.w: Strikes from behind land with far greater force against it.
